title: Predictive slot reservation and KV-tenant throttling to stabilize microbatching under sustained spikes
creator: Emily Chen
description: Summary: In recent sustained high-QPS incidents we've observed microbatch oscillation where admission thresholds chase transient spikes and GPU/KV memory thrash, increasing P95 latency and token cost. This ticket proposes a two-pronged stabilization strategy: (1) short-horizon predictive slot reservation that proactively reserves microbatch slots based on rolling request-rate forecasts and token-distribution heuristics; and (2) per-tenant soft KV cache throttles (KV-tenant throttling) to avoid single-tenancy hot-shrinking of GPU cache at cluster scale. The goal is reduced oscillation, more stable headroom, and fewer emergency evictions under multi-tenant load.
design_decision_summary: We will augment the admission-controller with a light-weight AR(2)-style rate forecaster and a token-demographic estimator to create a predictive reservation window (200-500ms horizon). Reservations allocate ephemeral slot credits that bias admission towards smoothing rather than maximizing immediate fill. Separately, a soft quota layer on KV cache per-tenant will enforce a reclaimable working set budget and a burstable token bucket that decays after idle periods. Admission will consult both predicted slot availability and tenant KV headroom before committing a microbatch; when headroom below threshold, requests may be routed to a compatible smaller model or degraded path.
implementation_notes:
- Forecasting: 250ms sliding window, exponential smoothing tuned to P95 arrival variance. Lightweight to avoid CPU overhead.
- Slot credits: integer credits representing microbatch slots; credits issued proportional to forecasted QPS and suppressed by current GPU headroom.
- KV quotas: soft quota per tenant implemented as approximate LRU watermarks + burst token bucket. When soft quota exceeded, mark entries for background eviction and tag tenant as throttled.
- Admission flow: (1) estimate forecasted incoming tokens; (2) check predicted free slots; (3) check tenant KV headroom/burst tokens; (4) accept/queue/reroute.
- Fallbacks: route to smaller-quantized model variant, or return 503 with retry-after when safe fallback unavailable.
experiment_plan: 1) Canary: rollout to 5% of serving nodes in staging under synthetic high-QPS trace for 48h. 2) Measure baseline vs canary on metrics above and overall cost per token. 3) If P95 latency reduces >10% and evictions drop >30% without increased error rate, expand to 25% then to 100% in controlled ramp. 4) Run chaos test: simultaneous KV hot-tenant and global spike to validate graceful degradation.
rollout_plan: Canary -> Gradual ramp with metric gates (p95 latency, eviction rate, failed admissions). Auto rollback triggers if error rate >0.5% or p95 latency regresses beyond 5% of baseline.
testing: Unit tests for forecasting and slot-credit logic, integration tests with mock KV cache to validate soft-quota behavior, load tests with previously captured traffic traces (incident-2026-02-18 trace set), and end-to-end latency/cost runs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Forecast model overfits short burst and blocks legitimate spikes. Mitigation: conservative smoothing + upper bound on credits; require sustained trend for aggressive reservations.
Risk: KV soft quotas could starve heavy-paying tenants. Mitigation: quotas are soft with configurable priority tiers; emergency overrides for enterprise contracts.
Risk: CPU overhead from forecasting on hot path. Mitigation: implement forecasting in C++ fast-path with vectorized ops and run per-shard rather than per-request.
Risk: Increased complexity in admission-controller. Mitigation: feature flag and observability surface; gradual rollout and runbook updates.
